items.title: A degree-uniform polynomial edge lift with the strong edge norm
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $p\in\mathbb N_0$, let $T=\{(x,y):x>0,\ y>0,\ x+y<1\}$, and let $q$ be a real polynomial of degree at most $p$ satisfying $q(0)=q(1)=0$. Define the polynomial $R(t)=q(t)/t$ by cancellation at $t=0$, and put
$$
Lq(x,y)=q(x)-xR(1-y).
$$
Then $Lq\in\mathbb P_p(T)$, it equals $q$ on $y=0$, and it vanishes on $x=0$ and $x+y=1$. Moreover,
$$
\|Lq\|_{H^1(T)}\le4\|q'\|_{L^2(0,1)},
$$
independently of $p$. Permuting the three vertices gives the same bound, up to one fixed constant, for each reference edge. If $K$ is a shape-regular affine triangle, $E$ is an edge of length $\ell_E$, and $h_K=\operatorname{diam}(K)$, the transported lift satisfies
$$
|L_Eq|_{H^1(K)}\le C_\gamma\ell_E^{1/2}\|\partial_\tau q\|_{L^2(E)},\qquad \|L_Eq\|_{L^2(K)}\le C_\gamma h_K\ell_E^{1/2}\|\partial_\tau q\|_{L^2(E)}.
$$
Consequently continuous polynomial data on the three edges of a triangle, each of degree at most the cell degree, have a polynomial extension of that cell degree. The estimate uses the strong $H^1$ edge norm and asserts no optimal $H^{1/2}$ trace-lifting bound.

items.title: An ordinary derivative controls the Legendre tail with a factorial ratio
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice for the $k\ge1$ branch. Let $P_n$ be the real Legendre polynomial normalized by $P_n(1)=1$, and let $\Pi_N$ be the $L^2(-1,1;\mathbb R)$ orthogonal projection onto $\mathbb P_N(-1,1)$. For every integer $k\ge1$, every integer $N\ge k-1$, and every real-valued $f\in H^k(-1,1)$,

$$
\|f-\Pi_Nf\|_{L^2(-1,1)}\le\left(\frac{(N+1-k)!}{(N+1+k)!}\right)^{1/2}\|f^{(k)}\|_{L^2(-1,1)}.
$$

For $k=0$, every integer $N\ge0$, and $f\in L^2(-1,1)$, $\|f-\Pi_Nf\|_2\le\|f\|_2$. For $n,m\ge k$ the repeated derivative orthogonality identity is

$$
\int_{-1}^1(1-x^2)^kP_n^{(k)}(x)P_m^{(k)}(x)\,dx=\frac{2}{2n+1}\frac{(n+k)!}{(n-k)!}\,\delta_{nm}.
$$

items.title: Analytic derivative bounds give exponential polynomial approximation on a triangle
items.statement:
Let $S$ be the closed reference triangle $\overline T$, where $T=\{x,y>0,x+y<1\}$, or the closed interval $[0,1]$, and let $f:S\to\mathbb R$ be real-valued. Write $\mathbb P_p(S)$ for restrictions of real polynomials of total degree at most $p$ on the triangle and degree at most $p$ on the interval. Say that $f$ is smooth up to $S$ when every partial derivative on the interior has a continuous extension to $S$. Suppose that for some $M>0$ and $A\ge1$,
$$
\|D^\alpha f\|_{L^\infty(S)}\le M A^{|\alpha|}|\alpha|!\qquad\text{for every multi-index }\alpha.
$$
Use $\|g\|_{W^{1,\infty}(S)}:=\|g\|_{L^\infty(S)}+\sum_{i=1}^{\dim S}\|\partial_i g\|_{L^\infty(S)}$. Then constants $C,b>0$, depending only on $A$ and the fixed reference domain, satisfy
$$
\inf_{q\in\mathbb P_p(S)}\|f-q\|_{W^{1,\infty}(S)}\le CM e^{-bp}\qquad(p\ge1).
$$
For the interval branch there is also an endpoint-preserving polynomial $J_pf\in\mathbb P_p([0,1])$ whose derivative is the $L^2$ orthogonal projection of $f'$ onto $\mathbb P_{p-1}$. It satisfies $\|(J_pf)'\|_2\le\|f'\|_2$ and $\|f-J_pf\|_{H^1}\le CM e^{-bp}$ after changing $C,b$ by constants depending only on $A$.

items.title: Weighted analytic polygon functions have corner decay and scaled analytic bounds
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^2$ be a bounded open polygonal domain with finitely many straight sides and corner set $\mathcal C=\{c_1,\ldots,c_m\}$, with interior angle at each corner strictly between $0$ and $2\pi$. Let $0\le\beta_i<1$ and write $\Phi_\gamma(x)=\prod_{i=1}^m|x-c_i|^{\gamma_i}$ for a vector $\gamma\in[0,\infty)^m$. For integer $k\ge2$, define

$$
\|v\|_{H^{k,2}_\beta(\Omega)}^2=\|v\|_{H^1(\Omega)}^2+\sum_{j=2}^k\sum_{|\alpha|=j}\|\Phi_{\beta+j-2}D^\alpha v\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2,
$$

where $(\beta+j-2)_i=\beta_i+j-2$ and a zero exponent contributes the factor one. Let $u\in H^{k,2}_\beta(\Omega)$ for every integer $k\ge2$, with real-valued weak derivatives, and suppose constants $C_u,d_u>0$ satisfy

$$
\left\|\Phi_{\beta+j-2}\sum_{|\alpha|=j}|D^\alpha u|\right\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\le C_ud_u^{j-2}(j-2)!\qquad(j\ge2).
$$

For each fixed $0<a<\min_i(1-\beta_i)$ there are constants $C,A,R>0$ such that the weak class of $u$ has a unique representative $\widetilde u\in C(\overline\Omega)$, smooth up to every open side away from corners, and for $0<r=|x-c_i|<R$,

$$
|\widetilde u(x)-\widetilde u(c_i)|\le Cr^a,\qquad |D^\alpha\widetilde u(x)|\le CA^{|\alpha|}|\alpha|!r^{a-|\alpha|}\quad(|\alpha|\ge1).
$$

On every compact subset of $\overline\Omega\setminus\mathcal C$, the derivatives satisfy ordinary factorial bounds $|D^\alpha u|\le C_0A_0^{|\alpha|}|\alpha|!$. On every shape-regular affine triangle $K\subset\Omega$ whose closure avoids $\mathcal C$ and whose ratio $h_K/\operatorname{dist}(K,\mathcal C)$ is bounded above and below by fixed positive constants, where $\operatorname{dist}(K,\mathcal C)=\inf_{x\in K,c\in\mathcal C}|x-c|$, set $r_K=\min(R,\operatorname{dist}(K,\mathcal C))$. After subtracting a suitable constant from the pullback $\widehat u$ to the reference triangle of [[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]], $\|D^\alpha\widehat u\|_\infty\le C A_1^{|\alpha|}|\alpha|!r_K^a$ for every multi-index $\alpha$, with constants uniform over this family. If a shape-regular triangle $K\subset\Omega$ of diameter $h<R$ has a corner $c_i$ as a vertex, its vertex affine interpolant $a_K$ satisfies

$$
|u-a_K|_{H^1(K)}\le Ch^a,\qquad \|u-a_K\|_{L^2(K)}\le Ch^{a+1}.
$$

items.title: Constructive ordinary Sobolev polynomial approximation on triangles
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $T=\{(x,y):x>0,\ y>0,\ x+y<1\}$, let $r\ge5$ be an integer, let $p\ge2r-4$ be an integer, and put $n=\lfloor p/2\rfloor$ and
$$
\eta_{n,r}=\left(\frac{(n-r+3)!}{(n+r-5)!}\right)^{1/2}.
$$
There is a bounded linear map $A_{p,r}:H^r(T;\mathbb R)\to\mathbb P_p(T;\mathbb R)$, where $\mathbb P_p(T;\mathbb R)$ is the restriction of real polynomials in $(x,y)$ of total degree at most $p$. It is explicitly defined in the proof from the reference-simplex extension, a unique moment polynomial, and finite Legendre projections, and satisfies
$$
\|u-A_{p,r}u\|_{H^2(T)}\le C_r\eta_{n,r}|u|_{H^r(T)}.
$$
Here $C_r$ is independent of $p$ and is the product of a fixed reference extension bound, the reference moment-projection bound, and an absolute tensor-projection constant; no useful growth bound in $r$ is asserted. For a shape-regular affine triangle $K$ of diameter $h_K$, affine transport gives
$$
\left(\sum_{j=0}^2h_K^{2j-2}|u-A_{K,p,r}u|_{H^j(K)}^2\right)^{1/2}\le C_{r,\gamma}\eta_{n,r}h_K^{r-1}|u|_{H^r(K)}.
$$
If $p\ge4(r-2)$, then $\eta_{n,r}\le(4/p)^{r-4}$. This is a conservative ordinary Sobolev rate; it is neither an optimal $p^{-(r-1)}$ estimate nor an analytic growth estimate for $C_r$.

items.title: Constructive varying-degree triangle interpolation in unweighted H1
items.statement:
Assume Full Choice. Let $\mathcal T$ be a finite matching shape-regular affine triangulation in two dimensions, let each cell $K$ have an arbitrary finite total degree $p_K\ge1$, and let $u\in C(\overline\Omega;\mathbb R)$ satisfy $u|_K\in H^2(K)$ for every cell. For every edge $E$, let $\tau_E$ be either unit tangent direction and write $\partial_{\tau_E}v=\nabla v\cdot\tau_E$. For an interior edge $E=K\cap K'$, set $p_E=\min(p_K,p_{K'})$; for a boundary edge of $K$, set $p_E=p_K$. Put $m_K=\min_{E\subset\partial K}p_E$. There is a linear interpolant $I_{\mathcal T,p}u$ in the trace-matching space of [[def-hp-variable-degree-spaces-on-matching-meshes]]. It preserves any zero boundary edge data: if $u$ vanishes on a boundary edge, so does $I_{\mathcal T,p}u$. For every $q\in\mathbb P_{m_K}(K;\mathbb R)$,

$$
|u-I_{\mathcal T,p}u|_{H^1(K)}\le |u-q|_{H^1(K)}+C_\gamma\sum_{E\subset\partial K}\left(\ell_E^{-1/2}\|u-q\|_{L^2(E)}+\ell_E^{1/2}\|\partial_{\tau_E}(u-q)\|_{L^2(E)}\right),
$$

and

$$
h_K^{-1}\|u-I_{\mathcal T,p}u\|_{L^2(K)}+|u-I_{\mathcal T,p}u|_{H^1(K)} \le C_\gamma\left(h_K^{-1}\|u-q\|_{L^2(K)}+|u-q|_{H^1(K)}+\sum_{E\subset\partial K}\left(\ell_E^{-1/2}\|u-q\|_{L^2(E)}+\ell_E^{1/2}\|\partial_{\tau_E}(u-q)\|_{L^2(E)}\right)\right).
$$

The constant is independent of the degrees and their ratios. In particular, if integer $r\ge5$, $m_K\ge2r-4$, $n_K=\lfloor m_K/2\rfloor$, and $u|_K\in H^r(K)$, then

$$
|u-I_{\mathcal T,p}u|_{H^1(K)}\le C_{r,\gamma}h_K^{r-1}\left(\frac{(n_K-r+3)!}{(n_K+r-5)!}\right)^{1/2}|u|_{H^r(K)}.
$$

For $m_K\ge4(r-2)$ the factorial factor is at most $(4/m_K)^{r-4}$. The effective degree $m_K$ records the lowest degree among the shared edge traces; no rate independent of neighboring trace degrees is asserted.

items.title: Exponential hp energy convergence for weighted-analytic polygon corners
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^2$ be a bounded polygonal open domain with finite corner set $\mathcal C=\{c_1,\ldots,c_m\}$ and weights $0\le\beta_i<1$. For $\gamma\in[0,\infty)^m$ define $\Phi_\gamma(x)=\prod_i|x-c_i|^{\gamma_i}$; $\beta+j-2$ means componentwise addition. For integer $k\ge2$, define

$$
\|v\|_{H^{k,2}_\beta(\Omega)}^2=\|v\|_{H^1(\Omega)}^2+\sum_{j=2}^k\sum_{|\alpha|=j}\|\Phi_{\beta+j-2}D^\alpha v\|_2^2.
$$

Let $B^2_\beta(\Omega)$ consist of real-valued functions in every $H^{k,2}_\beta(\Omega)$ for which some $C_u,d_u>0$ satisfy

$$
\left\|\Phi_{\beta+k-2}\sum_{|\alpha|=k}|D^\alpha u|\right\|_2\le C_ud_u^{k-2}(k-2)!\qquad(k\ge2).
$$

Let $(\mathcal T_k)_{k\ge1}$ be nested finite matching shape-regular affine triangulations of $\Omega$, with at most $C_0k$ triangles. Write $h_T=\operatorname{diam}(T)$ and $\operatorname{dist}(T,\mathcal C)=\inf_{x\in T,c\in\mathcal C}|x-c|$. Assume a fixed $0<\sigma<1$ and $C_1>0$ satisfy

$$
\sigma\le\frac{h_T}{\operatorname{dist}(T,\mathcal C)}\le\sigma^{-1}\quad(\overline T\cap\mathcal C=\varnothing),\qquad h_T\le C_1\sigma^k\quad(\overline T\cap\mathcal C\ne\varnothing).
$$

Let $p_k\in\mathbb N$ be uniform total polynomial degrees with $c_0k\le p_k\le c_1k$ for fixed $0<c_0\le c_1$. For a fixed union $\Gamma_D$ of polygon edges, let $V_k$ be the space of broken piecewise-$\mathbb P_{p_k}$ functions whose polynomial traces agree on every interior edge and vanish on the boundary edges in $\Gamma_D$; put $N_k=\dim V_k$. This is the corresponding subspace of the variable-degree space in [[def-hp-variable-degree-spaces-on-matching-meshes]].
For this smoother class, the boundary condition means that the unique continuous representative supplied by [[lem-hp-weighted-analytic-corner-pointwise-control]] vanishes pointwise on the edges in $\Gamma_D$; no zero condition is imposed on the other edges. If $u\in B^2_\beta(\Omega)$ satisfies this boundary condition, then constants $C,b>0$, independent of $k$, satisfy

$$
\inf_{v_k\in V_k}\|\nabla(u-v_k)\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\le Ce^{-bN_k^{1/3}}.
$$

For a bounded coercive conforming Galerkin problem on a Hilbert space $V\subset H^1(\Omega)$ containing $u$, with $V_k\subset V$ and norm equivalent to the gradient seminorm on $V$, Céa's estimate gives the same exponential rate for the energy error, with its actual $M/\alpha$ and norm-equivalence factors included. The constants may depend on the polygon, weights, weighted analytic bounds, mesh shape and grading constants, degree constants, $\Gamma_D$, and the Galerkin coercivity and norm-equivalence constants.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathcal T$ be any finite matching shape-regular affine triangulation of a bounded polygonal open set $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^2$, with shape bound $\gamma$ and arbitrary degrees $p_K\ge1$. Set $p_E=\min(p_K,p_{K'})$ on an interior edge, $p_E=p_K$ on a boundary edge, and $m_K=\min_{E\subset\partial K}p_E$. Thus the effective degree retains neighboring shared-trace restrictions, without a bound on degree ratios.

Choose $\chi=1$ and $V=H^1(\Omega)$, or $\chi=0$ and $V=H_0^1(\Omega)$, with Hilbert norm
$$\|v\|_V^2=|v|_{H^1(\Omega)}^2+\chi\|v\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2.$$
Let $V_{\mathcal T,p}$ be the corresponding conforming hp space, imposing zero boundary traces in the $\chi=0$ branch. Suppose the real bilinear form $a$ and real linear functional $F$ satisfy
$$|a(v,w)|\le M_a\|v\|_V\|w\|_V,\qquad a(v,v)\ge\alpha_a\|v\|_V^2,\qquad \alpha_a>0,$$
with $F$ bounded. Let $u\in V$ be the variational solution and $u_{\mathcal T,p}$ its conforming Galerkin solution. Suppose $u\in C(\overline\Omega)$ and $u|_K\in H^2(K)$; in the zero-boundary branch its continuous representative vanishes on the boundary edges.

For any cellwise comparison polynomials $q_K\in\mathbb P_{m_K}(K)$ put $w_K=u-q_K$ and
$$J_K(q_K)=|w_K|_{H^1(K)}+\sum_{E\subset\partial K}\left(\ell_E^{-1/2}\|w_K\|_{L^2(E)}+\ell_E^{1/2}\|\partial_{\tau_E}w_K\|_{L^2(E)}\right),\qquad R_K(q_K)=h_K^{-1}\|w_K\|_{L^2(K)}+J_K(q_K).$$
Then the actual energy-space error obeys
$$\|u-u_{\mathcal T,p}\|_V\le\frac{M_a}{\alpha_a}C_\gamma\left(\sum_{K\in\mathcal T}\bigl[J_K(q_K)^2+\chi h_K^2R_K(q_K)^2\bigr]\right)^{1/2}.$$
This comparison estimate applies to every degree assignment and the stated piecewise $H^2$ inputs; the comparison polynomials need not match across edges.

For any cellwise integers $s_K\ge2$ with $m_K\ge s_K-1$ and $u|_K\in H^{s_K}(K)$, this also gives the general h-refinement bound
$$\|u-u_{\mathcal T,p}\|_V\le\frac{M_a}{\alpha_a}\left(\sum_K C_{s_K,\gamma}^2(1+\chi h_K^2)h_K^{2(s_K-1)}|u|_{H^{s_K}(K)}^2\right)^{1/2}.$$
In particular every assignment $p_K\ge1$ admits the piecewise $H^2$ estimate with $s_K=2$.

For the additional explicit p-dependent refinement, let integers $r_K\ge5$ satisfy $m_K\ge2r_K-4$, assume $u|_K\in H^{r_K}(K)$, and put $n_K=\lfloor m_K/2\rfloor$ and
$$\eta_{K}=\left(\frac{(n_K-r_K+3)!}{(n_K+r_K-5)!}\right)^{1/2}.$$
There are constants $C_{r_K,\gamma}$ independent of all diameters, degrees and degree ratios such that
$$\|u-u_{\mathcal T,p}\|_V\le\frac{M_a}{\alpha_a}\left(\sum_{K\in\mathcal T}C_{r_K,\gamma}^2(1+\chi h_K^2)h_K^{2(r_K-1)}\eta_K^2|u|_{H^{r_K}(K)}^2\right)^{1/2}.$$
If $m_K\ge4(r_K-2)$, one may replace $\eta_K$ by $(4/m_K)^{r_K-4}$. For a common regularity $r$, this displays local $h_K^{r-1}$ and the proved conservative trace-degree factor $m_K^{-(r-4)}$. It does not claim the optimal $p^{-(r-1)}$ rate or any bound on growth of $C_{r,\gamma}$ as $r\to\infty$. The separate fixed-mesh tensor-analytic and weighted-corner exponential results remain independent branches.

items.title: GLL spectral-element energy error retains the quadrature defect
items.statement: Applies the first Strang estimate to the affine tensor GLL form, proves uniform stability from the top-mode estimate, and leaves variable-coefficient aliasing as an explicit bounded consistency-defect term.

references.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Part VI, Chapter 27, Error analysis with variational crimes
references.locator: §§27.1–27.3, printed pp. 1–8: the first Strang estimate and exact consistency defects.

references.title: Joachim Schöberl, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations
references.locator: Chapter 25: variational crimes, stability, and consistency-defect context.

title: hp finite elements and spectral elements — Examples

items.title: A degree-independent SIPDG penalty loses coercivity
items.statement: On two unit intervals, a Legendre endpoint reproducing kernel gives a one-face SIPDG test with quadratic energy gamma-p^2/4, which is negative for p^2>4 gamma.

references.title: Tim Warburton and Jan S. Hesthaven, On the Constants in hp-Finite Element Trace Inverse Inequalities
references.locator: §§2–4, pp. 3–14: sharp p-dependent polynomial endpoint and face inverse trace constants.

references.title: Leszek F. Demkowicz, Mathematical Theory of Finite Elements
references.locator: §3.1.4, printed pp. 64–68: hierarchical p-version bases; the explicit SIPDG witness is proved locally.

items.title: An analytic box solution has exponential Galerkin p convergence
items.statement: Applies the explicit reference-cell derivative bound to u(x)=exp(mu x) on a fixed interval and records the resulting geometric H1 p-error rate and energy-error transfer.

references.title: Joachim Schöberl, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, p-version FEM
references.locator: §§30.1–30.4: Legendre projection and exponential p-approximation context; the example uses the local explicit estimate.

references.title: Leszek F. Demkowicz, Mathematical Theory of Finite Elements
references.locator: §3.1.4, printed pp. 64–68: p-refinement spaces and hierarchical polynomial degrees.

items.title: The degree-two GLL mass matrix changes only its highest Legendre mode
items.statement: Computes the exact and GLL mass of P_p, verifies the ratio 2+1/p, and checks exactness on every lower Legendre mode and cross term.

references.title: Lloyd N. Trefethen, Short note on the mass matrix for Gauss-Lobatto grid points
references.locator: §§2–3, pp. 2–6: the highest Legendre coefficient gives the rank-one mass correction.

references.title: Lucas Johannes Petrus Timmermans, Analysis of Spectral Element Methods with Application to Incompressible Flow
references.locator: §2.2.4, PDF pp. 35–37: GLL mass matrix in the nodal basis.
